features.name: Interpreter
hints: I'm a polyglot who never appears on the invite list.
I let people in one meeting speak and listen in different languages.
I do speech-to-speech, not just translated captions.
Find me in a Teams meeting under More actions, then Language and speech.
I can even simulate your own voice when I interpret what you say.
features.description: A Teams agent that interprets what people say in real time, so everyone in a meeting or call can speak and listen in the language they choose. It can even use a simulated version of your own voice.
features.why: Language stops being a barrier to joining the conversation, so global teams can meet live without waiting for translated notes or squinting at text captions.
features.prompt: I run a weekly project meeting with colleagues who speak English, Japanese and Portuguese. Explain how to turn on Interpreter in Teams and how each person sets the language they speak and the language they want to hear.
features.learnLabel: Microsoft Learn: Interpreter agent in Teams

features.name: Agent Store
hints: Think shop window, but for helpers rather than products.
People come to me to discover assistants from Microsoft, trusted partners and their own colleagues.
If your admin wants a say, my button says Request approval instead of Add.
Find me by choosing Agents in Copilot's left navigation, then All agents.
I'm the central hub in Copilot for finding and adding agents.
features.description: The central hub in Microsoft Copilot where people discover and add agents from Microsoft, partners and their own organisation. Admins decide which agents are approved, blocked or removed.
features.why: Instead of helpful agents being scattered across links and emails, there's one governed place to find them, so good ones get used and risky ones can be controlled.
features.prompt: I'm new to agents. Show me which agents I can add from the Agent Store for research, data analysis and meeting notes, and explain what each one does.
features.learnLabel: Microsoft Learn: Agent Store in Microsoft Copilot

features.name: Agent Builder
hints: No code, no problem: describe what you want in plain English and I'll set up the rest.
I live right inside Copilot, so makers needn't leave the chat to create their own helper.
I can ground an agent in files, sites, chats and meetings, then let you try it out.
I have a Configure tab and a Try it tab, but for actions and workflows you copy my agent to Copilot Studio.
I'm the lightweight builder of agents inside Copilot, sometimes nicknamed Copilot Studio lite.
features.description: A lightweight, chat-driven tool inside Microsoft Copilot for creating your own agents. Describe the agent in plain language, add knowledge, test it, then share or publish it.
features.why: Anyone can turn a repeatable question-and-answer job into a shared helper without waiting for a developer, which puts automation in the hands of the people who know the work.
features.prompt: Create an agent called Leave Buddy that answers staff questions about our leave policy. Use the HR policy document I've uploaded as its only source and keep answers short and friendly.

features.name: Copilot Studio
hints: I'm a workshop where makers build helpers without needing to be developers.
Low-code is my thing: describe, connect and test, then publish to Teams, websites and Copilot.
I bring together agents, workflows and agent flows, plus knowledge, tools and analytics.
I absorbed the capabilities of the old Power Virtual Agents.
Learn calls me a graphical, low-code studio for building and managing AI-powered agents.
features.description: A graphical, low-code studio for building and managing AI-powered agents and workflows. Makers connect knowledge and tools, then publish to channels like Teams, Microsoft Copilot, websites and mobile apps.
features.why: Departments and citizen makers can automate real work and customer conversations, with the governance, analytics and testing a business needs.
features.prompt: I'm planning an agent in Copilot Studio that answers staff questions about travel policy and raises an approval request. List the knowledge sources, tools and test questions I should set up first.
features.learnLabel: Microsoft Learn: What is Copilot Studio?

features.name: Declarative Agents
hints: I describe what to do rather than doing it myself: there's no custom orchestrator inside me.
I run on Copilot's own brain, using its orchestrator and models.
I'm defined by a purpose, instructions, knowledge and capabilities, kept in a manifest.
Agent Builder makes me for low-code makers; the Agents Toolkit makes me for pro-code developers.
My cousin the custom engine agent brings its own orchestration; I simply declare what I need.
features.description: Agents defined by configuration rather than custom code: you declare their purpose, instructions, knowledge and capabilities, and Microsoft 365 Copilot's own orchestrator and models do the rest.
features.why: You get tailored, governed assistants that feel native in Copilot, without building or hosting your own AI stack.
features.prompt: I'm a developer. Outline the parts of a declarative agent manifest for a sales-playbook assistant: name, instructions, knowledge sources and capabilities, plus how I'd test it before publishing.

features.name: Custom Engine Agents
hints: I bring my own brain to the party instead of borrowing Copilot's.
My makers keep full control of orchestration, models and data connections.
I can be built low-code in Copilot Studio, pro-code with the Agents Toolkit, or by bringing a Foundry agent along.
Once approved I turn up in the Agent Store, and I can message people proactively.
Unlike my declarative cousin, I run on an engine my makers choose.
features.description: Agents that bring their own orchestration, AI models and data integrations into Microsoft 365 Copilot, Teams and other channels, instead of using Microsoft 365 Copilot's orchestrator.
features.why: When a business needs its own models, workflows or integrations, it can still deliver the result inside Copilot, where people already work.
features.prompt: I'm an architect. Compare when to build a declarative agent versus a custom engine agent for a claims-triage assistant, covering orchestration, models, hosting and licensing questions.

features.name: Copilot Connectors
hints: I'm a bridge to data that lives beyond Microsoft 365.
Permissions are my superpower: people only see what they could already see in the source.
Some of me index content into the graph; others fetch it live over MCP without indexing.
Prebuilt versions of me cover popular tools like Salesforce, ServiceNow and Confluence.
I used to be called Microsoft Graph connectors until Build 2025 gave me a new name.
features.description: Connectors that bring external data from SaaS apps, file shares, databases and on-premises systems into Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Search. They either index content into Microsoft Graph or fetch it live, while respecting source permissions.
features.why: Copilot's answers are only as good as the knowledge it can reach. Connectors bring the rest of the business into the conversation, safely.
features.prompt: We store our product documentation in Confluence. Explain how Copilot connectors could make that knowledge available in Copilot, including who needs to configure what and how permissions are respected.

features.name: Agent Flows
hints: Same input, same output: predictability is my whole personality.
I start with a trigger and need at least one action.
Agents can call me as a tool, and I can include AI steps and human approvals.
A classic example of my work: extract invoice data, validate it, then route it for approval.
A Power Automate cloud flow can be converted into me, and I live in Copilot Studio.
features.description: Deterministic automations built in Copilot Studio from a trigger and actions, optionally with AI steps, human approvals and connectors. Agents can call them as tools.
features.why: Some work needs the same result every time. Agent flows give agents a reliable way to handle those steps.
features.prompt: Help me design an agent flow in Copilot Studio that takes a submitted invoice, extracts the key fields, checks them against our supplier list and sends an approval request. List the trigger and each action.

features.name: Computer Use
hints: I click and type so the humans don't have to.
I work with websites and desktop apps on a Windows machine, even ones with no API.
I pair vision with reasoning, so I keep going when a button moves or a screen changes.
My chat shows my reasoning and screenshots, and Stop testing halts everything on the machine.
Think of me as the tool that lets an agent operate the computer itself.
features.description: A Copilot Studio tool that lets an agent operate websites and desktop apps on a Windows machine by seeing the screen and using a virtual mouse and keyboard, following instructions given in plain language.
features.why: Plenty of business systems have no API. This lets agents automate those screens too, without brittle scripts that break when the interface changes.
features.prompt: Plan how an agent that can use a computer could enter approved purchase orders into our legacy accounting app. Which steps could it handle, and what should a person review?
features.learnLabel: Microsoft Learn: Computer use in Copilot Studio

features.name: Multi-Agent Orchestration
hints: I'm about teamwork between agents, not one agent doing everything.
A main agent can hand a conversation to a specialist, then carry on afterwards.
My helpers can be lightweight children inside the agent, other agents in the environment, or external ones.
Learn warns that adding more agents adds latency and widens testing and governance.
Several agents, one conductor: I'm Copilot Studio's way of orchestrating them.
features.description: Copilot Studio's ability for a main agent to delegate work to other agents: child agents inside it, other Copilot Studio agents, or external agents over A2A or from Foundry.
features.why: Splitting a big solution into focused agents keeps each one simpler to build, test and govern, and lets teams reuse specialists.
features.prompt: We want one front-door agent that routes to separate HR, IT and finance agents. Explain how multi-agent orchestration in Copilot Studio could work and the trade-offs of child versus connected agents.

features.name: Copilot Tuning
hints: I teach a model your house style, using your own data.
What I tune stays private to you, inside the Microsoft 365 trust boundary.
I can adapt the context I'm given, the tools I use or the model's own weights.
I make agents that sound like your organisation for jobs like drafting documents and answering expert questions.
Announced at Build 2025, I'm all about turning a general model into your own.
features.description: An early-access capability for tuning models on your own organisational data to build task-specific agents that reflect your terminology, tone and quality standards, inside the Microsoft 365 trust boundary.
features.why: A generic model doesn't know how your firm writes or what good looks like. Tuning teaches agents your standards.
features.prompt: We're considering Copilot Tuning for contract drafting. List the data we'd need to gather, the review steps for quality, and the governance questions to ask before we start.

features.name: MCP Support
hints: I'm a standard handshake between agents and the tools they use.
I have three building blocks, tools, resources and prompts, and Copilot Studio supports two of them.
I ride on connector infrastructure, so data loss prevention and VNet integration still apply.
An agent needs generative orchestration before it can call my tools.
Spell out my three letters: Model, Context, Protocol.
features.description: Support for the open Model Context Protocol, so agents can discover and call tools and resources exposed by MCP servers. Copilot Studio can add existing servers or publish your own.
features.why: One open standard means agents can plug into many tools without custom glue for each, while makers keep enterprise controls.
features.prompt: Explain what an MCP server is and how I could add one to a Copilot Studio agent so it can look up open support tickets. Mention authentication and any admin controls.
features.learnLabel: Microsoft Learn: MCP in Copilot Studio

features.name: Agents Toolkit
hints: I changed my name but kept my toolbox.
I'm pro-code tooling: templates, debugging, provisioning and publishing for builders of agents and apps.
You'll find me in VS Code and Visual Studio, and I come with a command line too.
I'm free, and I play nicely with the Agents SDK, the Agents Playground and Azure AI Foundry.
Once I was Teams-flavoured; now I'm all about agents.
features.description: Microsoft's free pro-code toolkit, formerly Teams Toolkit, for building, debugging, testing and publishing agents and apps for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Teams and Microsoft 365.
features.why: Developers get one toolkit from first template to published agent, instead of stitching tools together.
features.prompt: I'm new to the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit. Walk me through creating, debugging and publishing a declarative agent that answers questions from our SharePoint product docs.

features.name: Researcher
hints: I'm not a quick-answer chatbot. I'd rather vanish for a while and come back with footnotes.
Hand me a big, thorny question and I'll comb through your work content and the open web.
I may ask clarifying questions first, so you can steer my plan before I begin.
Find me under Agents in the left navigation, or @-mention me in a regular Copilot chat.
I was announced alongside Analyst as a reasoning agent: complex question in, source-cited research report out.
features.description: A Copilot reasoning agent for big, complex questions. It may ask clarifying questions, then works through your files, emails, meetings, chats and the web, and returns an organised, source-cited report with charts and visuals.
features.why: It does the slow legwork of gathering and weighing sources across your work data and the web, so you start from a structured, cited report and spend your time on judgement.
features.prompt: Prepare a briefing on Contoso ahead of our renewal call on Friday. Look at our recent emails, meeting notes and shared files, plus current public news, and finish with three risks and three opportunities. Ask me any clarifying questions first.

features.name: Analyst
hints: Give me a messy pile of rows and columns and I'll coax a story out of it.
I reason through your question in as many steps as it takes, then report trends and outliers.
Behind the scenes I write and run Python, and you can watch the code in real time.
Find me under Agents in the left navigation; attach files with the '+' next to the prompt box.
Microsoft says I think like a skilled data scientist: I analyse your Excel and CSV files.
features.description: A Copilot reasoning agent that works like a data analyst. Attach spreadsheets or CSV files, ask a question, and it reasons step by step, runs Python you can watch, and returns insights with charts and tables.
features.why: Go from a raw data file to trends, outliers and charts without building formulas yourself. Because you can watch the code it runs, you can check the working before you trust the answer.
features.prompt: Using the attached files, identify our top-performing products based on customer engagement, flag any outliers, and chart the monthly trend. Explain your reasoning step by step so I can check it.
features.learnLabel: Microsoft Support: Get started with Analyst

features.name: Facilitator
hints: I'm the one at the table who watches the clock, so nobody else has to.
I keep a meeting on track by taking notes, answering questions and drafting documents as it happens.
Unlike Copilot in Teams, anything you ask me is visible to everyone in the meeting.
You'll find me on a meeting's Notes tab, in meeting chat via @-mention, and in Teams Rooms.
I'm the Teams agent that facilitates meetings with live notes everyone can edit, agenda timers and Word drafts.
features.description: An AI agent for Teams meetings and Teams Rooms that helps keep discussions on track. It keeps collaborative live notes, tracks agenda time, answers questions from meeting and web content, and can draft Word documents during or after the meeting.
features.why: Nobody gets stuck being the scribe, and everyone works from the same live notes, agenda and timer, so the conversation stays focused and on schedule.
features.prompt: @Facilitator Add 'budget review' and 'launch risks' to the agenda, then once we wrap up, draft a Word document of what we decided.

features.name: Planner Agent
hints: I'm assignable like any teammate, but you won't find me on the org chart.
Assign me a task and I'll draft the work, while you stay assigned too to follow along.
I can write status reports for the last week, fortnight, month or quarter, in a length you choose.
Board view can group tasks by AI agent progress: pending, assigned to me, couldn't complete, ready for review.
Formerly the Project Manager agent, I now carry Planner's name and a matching icon.
features.description: An AI agent built into Microsoft Planner that you can assign tasks to. It drafts the work for you to review, writes status reports from your plan data and, in premium plans, can turn a high-level goal into tasks.
features.why: Routine project admin, such as drafting task output and writing status updates, can be handed to an agent, leaving the team more time for the work that needs people.
features.prompt: Draft a one-page announcement of our new returns process: what changes, who is affected and the key dates. Use the policy document I've uploaded as your source and note anything you couldn't confirm.

features.name: Employee Self-Service agent
aliases: Employee Self-Service Agent in M365 Copilot
hints: I'm a head start, not a blank page: organisations add their own knowledge and systems.
People ask me about policies, benefits or a stubborn laptop, and I can raise a ticket.
I come with ready-made scenarios for Workday and ServiceNow: getting, creating and updating cases.
Staff meet me inside Microsoft Copilot, mobile app included, as an agent their organisation publishes.
Think HR and IT self-service, packaged as prebuilt agent starters that organisations deploy through Copilot Studio.
features.description: A prebuilt set of agent starters for HR and IT that organisations deploy through Copilot Studio. Employees ask questions in Microsoft Copilot, from policies and benefits to IT troubleshooting, and can take actions in systems such as Workday and ServiceNow.
features.why: Staff can ask a question or start an HR or IT request in the Copilot they already use, without hunting for the right portal, while organisations start from a prebuilt starter rather than building from scratch.
features.prompt: How much parental leave am I entitled to under our policy, and what do I need to submit? If a case needs to be raised, please start it for me.

features.name: Agent Registry
hints: I'm the admin's roll call, not the shop window.
I give admins one central place to monitor, manage and govern every agent available to their organisation.
My summary cards count everything, the ownerless and the unmanaged.
You'll find me in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Agents, then All Agents.
I'm the 'registry': one list of every agent your organisation can use, with owner, publisher type and status.
features.description: The Microsoft 365 admin center's central list of every agent available to your organisation, showing ownership, publisher type and status. Admins can filter and export it to monitor, manage and govern agents, and tenants with the right licence also see risk signals.
features.why: Agents can come from Microsoft, partners and colleagues, so IT needs one place to see what exists, who owns it and what's unmanaged. That visibility makes it easier to keep agents under control.
features.prompt: I'm a Microsoft 365 admin. Give me a weekly checklist for reviewing the agent registry: how to spot agents without owners or unmanaged agents, which filters to use, and what to do before blocking or deleting an agent.

features.name: Champion Program
hints: I'm a club for the colleague who always says, 'Here, let me show you.'
I'm for people who blend tech know-how with people skills to help colleagues adopt Microsoft 365 and Copilot.
My calls go by 'Driving Adoption', and recordings let you catch up on demand.
I'm filed under Training on Microsoft's Adoption site, yet I'm a network of peers, not a course.
A short sign-up form is all it takes to become a Champion yourself.
features.description: A free Microsoft community and resource hub for the people who help colleagues adopt Microsoft 365 and Copilot. Members get peer networking, an adoption asset library, Microsoft experts, community calls and a forum.
features.why: New tools stick when someone down the hall can show you how. The community gives those helpers peers, adoption assets and Microsoft experts, so good habits spread through the organisation.
features.prompt: I'm setting up an AI Champions network for about 800 staff. Help me draft a one-page role charter (purpose, expectations, what Champions don't do) and a short email inviting people to join.

features.name: Channel Agent
hints: I take my name from the place I live, not from a person.
I flag deadlines and answer questions about the work, as a domain expert for one team.
I draft status reports as Loop files, ready for your team to review and customise.
Unlike Facilitator, which belongs to a single meeting, I belong to one place where a team works.
A Teams channel can have only one of me: its own dedicated AI expert.
features.description: Gives a Teams channel its own AI expert, currently in public preview. It draws on the channel's messages, files and approved meeting summaries to answer questions, flag deadlines, draft status reports and create tasks.
features.why: Project knowledge often sits in scattered threads and files. A dedicated expert for the channel can answer questions from that material and draft status updates, so people spend less time chasing colleagues for the latest.
features.prompt: Draft this week's status report for our team: summarise progress since Monday, flag any deadlines at risk, and list the open tasks with their owners.

features.name: Copilot Academy
hints: I'm a school whose door is open by default: everyone with Microsoft 365 can walk in.
Microsoft has already curated my lessons, so nobody has to build an AI curriculum from scratch.
Admins with a Viva licence can duplicate me, swap in their own learning paths and publish to groups.
I'm sometimes mistaken for Microsoft Learn, but I live in Viva Learning and borrow its lessons.
Graduation caps optional: my name ends with 'Academy', and my lessons are all about AI.
features.description: Officially called Microsoft Copilot Academy, this is a ready-made, Microsoft-curated learning academy inside Viva Learning, with structured Copilot learning paths. Knowledge admins can restrict it to Copilot-licensed users, and admins with a Viva licence can duplicate and customise it.
features.why: People get more from Copilot when they know how to use it well. The Academy gives everyone ready-made lessons inside Viva Learning, and gives admins a head start on staff training.
features.prompt: I'm a Knowledge admin rolling out Copilot to 300 staff. Draft a plan for introducing Microsoft Copilot Academy in Viva Learning: who gets access, how to customise it for finance and sales, and a short Teams announcement.

features.name: Copilot Chat
hints: I'm not a search tab, a canvas or a notebook; I'm the one you simply talk to.
I answer, draft and summarise using the web and, with one toggle on, your work data.
Type a slash and I'll let you point me at one specific file, person or meeting.
I've swapped name tags: my first said 'Business', a later one said '365'.
I'm the Copilot you chat with, on the web, on your phone, and inside Teams and Outlook.
features.description: The conversational assistant in the Copilot app, Outlook, Teams and Office: speak or type a request and it drafts, summarises and answers using the web and, via Work IQ, your work data. Once called Business Chat, then Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.
features.why: Instead of hunting through inboxes and folders, you just ask. It can draft, summarise and answer from the web and the work you already have access to, so you spend your time deciding, not digging.
features.prompt: Goal: draft a 150-word update for my leadership team. Context: we're two weeks from launching our new onboarding portal. Details: friendly, plain English, flag one risk and one decision we need from them. Data: the launch plan file and last Tuesday's project meeting.

features.name: Copilot Control System
hints: I'm not a switch, a product or a licence - think of me as an umbrella.
I help IT and security teams secure, manage and measure Copilot and agents as they scale.
I rest on three pillars: security and governance, management, and measurement and reporting.
The admin center's Copilot > Settings page is where admins change things; I'm the bigger picture around it.
Microsoft's pages use two names for me, and one of them ends in 'System'.
features.description: Microsoft's umbrella framework of guides and tools for securing, managing and measuring Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat and Microsoft Copilot Studio, built on three pillars. Microsoft's pages use both 'Copilot Control System' and 'Copilot controls'.
features.why: Rolling Copilot and agents out across a whole company is smoother when security, settings and usage reporting follow one plan. IT gets clear guardrails, and the business can scale with confidence.
features.prompt: I'm the IT admin for a 2,000-person company about to roll out Microsoft 365 Copilot. Using the three pillars of Copilot controls (security and governance, management, measurement and reporting), draft a 30-60-90 day plan with owners and the first checks to run.

features.name: Copilot Create
aliases: Create in the Microsoft Copilot app
Create in the Microsoft 365 Copilot app
hints: I'm a workshop where a single sentence does the heavy lifting.
I turn what you describe into visuals or written drafts.
Whatever I make, you can edit it and save it to your Library.
Look behind the 'Apps and more' icon at the top left of the Copilot app.
My name is the verb for making something new: posters, banners, videos and more.
features.description: A creation hub in the Microsoft Copilot app. Describe an image, banner, poster, video, infographic, story or form, or start from a template, and Copilot makes it for you to edit and save to your Library.
features.why: Get a first draft of a visual or a written piece just by describing it, then refine it. Official Brand Kits help keep it on brand when your organisation provides one.
features.prompt: Create a wide banner for our customer webinar 'Budgeting basics' in a clean, friendly style, using calm blues and leaving space on the left for the title text.
features.learnLabel: Microsoft Support: Get started with Create

features.name: Copilot Dashboard
hints: Think of me as a four-part report card on an organisation's AI journey.
I help leaders judge if Copilot is landing: are people ready, using it, gaining from it, happy?
My readiness, adoption and impact pages each look back over the previous 28 days.
I'm often mixed up with the Microsoft 365 admin center's simpler Copilot usage reports, but I live elsewhere.
Find me in Viva Insights' left navigation, under a name ending in 'Dashboard'.
features.description: A Viva Insights dashboard that tracks four things: how ready your organisation is for Copilot, how people are adopting it, what impact it's having and how people feel about it. It covers Copilot Chat usage too.
features.why: Rolling out AI is easier to steer when readiness, usage, impact and feelings are visible in one place. Leaders can back what's working and show the value with evidence, not hunches.
features.prompt: Help me prepare a 10-minute update for our leadership team on Copilot adoption. Using the four categories in the Copilot Dashboard (readiness, adoption, impact and sentiment), outline the questions to answer, the numbers to show and the actions to recommend.

features.name: Copilot in Edge
hints: I do my work in plain sight, and you can grab the wheel whenever you like.
I can summarise the page you're on and compare it with your other open tabs.
I'll ask for your attention before buying, booking, sending an email or deleting a calendar event.
I'm not the Copilot app on Windows; I live inside a web browser instead.
Click my icon at the top right of Microsoft Edge to chat about the page you're on.
features.description: Copilot built into Microsoft Edge has a side pane that chats about the page you're on, summarises it and compares tabs. Browse with Copilot, which is experimental, can also click and type in your tabs while you watch.
features.why: Instead of juggling tabs and copy-pasting into another app, you can ask about the page in front of you. With a work account, enterprise data protection applies, shown by a shield icon.
features.prompt: Summarise this page in five bullet points, then compare it with my other open tabs and tell me which supplier has the best delivery terms.

features.name: Copilot in Forms
hints: I'm a ghostwriter for questions that other people will end up answering.
Describe what you want to find out and I'll propose a title, questions and answer options.
I can review a draft for leading or double-barrelled questions and suggest improvements.
I'm not the agent that makes surveys from chat; I'm built into the survey-and-quiz app itself.
Start a new survey or quiz in Microsoft Forms, describe it, and I'll draft the lot.
features.description: Describe the survey or quiz you need and Copilot drafts a title, questions and answer options. It can also review your questions, help you share the form, and summarise the responses into key findings and insights.
features.why: A blank form is slow to build and easy to get wrong. Copilot gives you a solid first draft, reviews your questions and turns piles of responses into insights you can act on.
features.prompt: Create a short employee pulse survey about workload, team communication and career growth. Keep the wording neutral and avoid leading or double-barrelled questions.

features.name: Copilot in Loop
hints: Part of my toolkit was boxed up on purpose; Microsoft plans to bring some back.
I can recap the changes made on a page.
In meetings I generate collaborative notes with suggested tasks, shareable as components.
Copilot Pages is built on the same technology as the app I live in.
Find me behind the upper-right Copilot button of a page in Microsoft's Loop app.
features.description: Copilot inside the Loop app lets licensed users ask web or work questions in a chat and insert answers onto a page, recap page changes, and generate collaborative notes in meetings. Microsoft has trimmed some features while aligning Loop with Copilot Pages.

On a site's Settings tab, my toggle's label mentions Microsoft Copilot, not my own name.
Admins flip me on, site by site, to curb discovery in organisation-wide search and Copilot answers.
features.description: A SharePoint Advanced Management setting that hides a site's content from organisation-wide search and Microsoft Copilot responses, and removes AI entry points on that site. Permissions don't change, so people with access can still open files directly.
features.why: Oversharing worries shouldn't stall your Copilot rollout. Admins can pull risky sites out of Copilot answers while owners review permissions, and nobody loses access to their files.
features.prompt: I'm a SharePoint admin preparing a phased Copilot rollout. Draft a plan for using Restricted Content Discovery on our Finance and HR sites: what it hides, what stays the same for people with access, and how I'd report on which sites have it turned on.

features.name: Restricted SharePoint Search
hints: I was more of a 'please use this entrance' sign than a locked door.
I was a short-term fix, meant only to buy admins time to audit site permissions.
My list topped out at 100 sites; a hub site counted as just one.
Microsoft has announced my retirement and pointed admins to a per-site setting instead.
I was the tenant setting that scoped organisation-wide search and Copilot to an allow list of chosen sites.
features.description: A short-term tenant setting that limited organisation-wide search and Copilot to an allow list of up to 100 SharePoint sites. Microsoft has announced its retirement: new enablement has been blocked since 31 July 2026, and Restricted Content Discovery is the recommended alternative.
features.why: It was a stopgap for pointing Copilot at reviewed sites, never a security lock, and Microsoft says its 100-site cap doesn't scale. Knowing that helps you choose the right controls today.
features.prompt: Our tenant already has a Restricted SharePoint Search allow list. Explain why Microsoft announced its retirement and what it never guaranteed, then draft a plan to move to Restricted Content Discovery for our sensitive sites, including how I'd review what's on the list today.

features.name: Scenario Library
hints: I'm a menu of 'what could AI do for us?' ideas, not a tool you switch on.
Teams unsure where to start with AI come to me to find their own corner of the business.
I'm sorted two ways: by what your team does, and by the industry you work in.
I live on Microsoft's Adoption site; my old name wore a Copilot badge, but I'm no longer Copilot-only.
My downloads include scenario kits and day-in-the-life guides, and my name suggests a bookshelf.
features.description: The Microsoft Scenario Library, formerly the Copilot Scenario Library, is a Microsoft Adoption website that organises AI scenarios by business function and industry, with downloadable scenario kits, scenario guides and day-in-the-life guides. Anyone can browse it, no licence needed.
features.why: Starting with AI is easier when you can see what it could do in your own role or industry. The library turns 'where do we begin?' into ideas and guides you can download.
features.prompt: I lead finance operations at a mid-size manufacturer and we're new to AI. Using Microsoft's Scenario Library as inspiration, suggest five Copilot scenarios for my team, what each would save us, and which one to pilot first.

features.name: Semantic Index
hints: No admin switches me on, and no admin can switch me off.
I help Copilot find conceptually related content, even when your exact words don't appear in it.
Hand me the word 'praise' and I'll widen it to elated, excited and amazed.
My organisation-wide version is generated from text-based SharePoint Online files.
I'm the 'semantic' counterpart to Microsoft Graph's lexical, keyword-based matching.
features.description: A vector-based index that sits alongside Microsoft Graph's keyword (lexical) index, helping Copilot find conceptually related content across your organisation. It understands synonyms and intent, only surfaces what a user can already access, and Microsoft switches it on automatically.
features.why: Searching by meaning means Copilot can find the right file even when you don't remember its exact words. Because it only shows content you can already open, better answers don't mean looser access.
features.prompt: I'm a Microsoft 365 admin. Explain how semantic indexing helps Copilot find relevant files, what I can and can't control (like the SharePoint 'Allow this site to appear in search results' setting), and how permissions limit what each user sees.
features.learnLabel: Microsoft Learn: Semantic indexing for Microsoft Copilot

features.name: SharePoint Advanced Management
hints: I'm a caretaker's keyring: lots of keys, one job, keeping the whole estate in order.
I help admins keep things tidy and tightly governed, so Copilot draws on the right content.
My tools tackle three worries: sprawl, lifecycle and oversharing, with inactive sites included.
Restricted access control and restricted content discovery both shelter under me; I'm the umbrella.
Say my acronym aloud and you get a friendly first name; 'Advanced' is in my full name.
features.description: A bundle of SharePoint admin center governance tools for taming content sprawl, managing the content lifecycle and preventing oversharing. It helps admins keep sites tidy and tightly governed so Copilot draws on the right content.
features.why: Employees get Copilot answers from the right content, with less chance of stumbling over files that were never meant for them. IT gets one toolkit to tidy and tighten sites.
features.prompt: I'm a SharePoint admin preparing for a Microsoft 365 Copilot rollout. Using SharePoint Advanced Management, draft a phased plan covering content sprawl, content lifecycle and oversharing, naming the SharePoint admin center area to visit for each step and who should own it.

features.name: Site Access Review
aliases: Data access governance site access review
hints: I'm IT handing the clipboard to whoever actually knows what's in each room.
I exist because compliance reasons stop IT admins seeing file-level detail inside a site.
I send each site's owner an email tailored to the problem, in words the admin can tweak.
I'm not Entra's group-and-app checkup: I start inside a report about overshared sites.
In the SharePoint admin center, admins follow my progress on a tab called 'My review requests'.
features.description: Lets admins hand an oversharing check to the owners of the affected SharePoint sites. From a data access governance report, an admin selects sites and sends each owner a tailored email; owners then review and update access themselves.
features.why: Compliance reasons stop IT seeing file-level detail, but site owners know their own content. Asking owners to check and tighten sharing puts the fix with the people best placed to make it.
features.prompt: I'm a SharePoint admin starting site access reviews from a data access governance report because several sites are shared with 'Everyone except external users'. Draft the email to site owners: why IT can't check their files, what to review, and a clear deadline.

features.name: Teams Meeting Recap
hints: I'm the goodie bag at the end of the party, not the party itself.
I let absentees catch up without juggling a pile of different apps.
Recording, transcript, shared files, agenda and follow-up tasks all end up together inside me.
I'm the box, not the brains: AI notes are just one thing I can hold.
Click 'View recap' on an event's thumbnail and I open.
features.description: The tab that appears in a Teams event's chat and calendar details once it has been recorded or transcribed. It gathers the recording, transcript, shared files, notes, agenda and follow-up tasks in one place, plus an AI summary where your licence includes it.
features.why: Missed the meeting, or can't remember what was agreed? Everything from the event sits in one place, so you can catch up quickly and find the bit that matters without chasing files or people.
features.prompt: I missed Tuesday's project review. Using its transcript and notes, list the decisions made, the follow-up tasks and who owns them, and flag anything that affects my team's deadlines.
features.learnLabel: Microsoft Support: Recap in Microsoft Teams

features.name: Teams Phone Agent
hints: I'm what you get when 'press 1 for sales' becomes an actual conversation.
I screen callers, answer common questions and book appointments, then route people where they need to go.
Unless an admin changes it, I introduce myself to callers as a virtual assistant.
I answer calls made to a resource account, not to one person's own line.
I'm the phone-answering AI that lives where auto attendants live: Voice, in the Teams admin center.
features.description: An AI-driven extension of Teams auto attendants that answers incoming calls to a resource account in human-like conversation. It screens callers, answers questions from approved sources, books appointments and routes calls to people, queues or Copilot Studio agents, without fixed menus.
features.why: Callers talk naturally instead of pressing through menus, and routine questions and bookings are handled without tying up staff, so people can focus on the calls that need them.
features.prompt: I'm a Teams admin setting up a Teams Phone Agent for our front desk. List what I need before I start (resource account, licences, greeting, Q&A sources) and draft a friendly greeting plus five common questions it should answer.

features.name: Copilot in Teams Rooms
hints: I put names to voices, and faces too, but only for people who opt in.
Thanks to me, meeting summaries and recaps can credit comments to the right person.
Switch me on under Settings, then Recognition; I typically learn your voice within a couple of meetings.
I'm easy to confuse with a recap's after-the-fact timeline, but I identify people live.
I'm what lets Teams Rooms devices tell a transcript who's who.
features.description: The AI side of Teams Rooms devices, centred on Intelligent Speaker. It uses opt-in voice and face profiles to identify who in the room is talking, so transcripts, recaps and Copilot can name who said what.
features.why: When people meet together around one device, knowing who said what makes summaries and recaps more useful. Comments can be credited to the right person by name.
features.prompt: I manage Teams Rooms devices. Draft a rollout checklist for Intelligent Speaker: what licence each room's resource account needs, how users opt in under Recognition, and what the CsTeamsAIPolicy settings control.
features.learnLabel: Microsoft Learn: Admin guide to Copilot in Teams
